excerpt: Every week of a 20-week marathon schedule in miles and km. For runners who've run a half and do 18-22 mi (29-35 km) a week; peaks at 45 mi (72 km).
body:
20 Week Marathon Training Plan (Miles & Km)

This 20 week marathon training plan is for runners who have finished a half marathon and currently run about 18–22 miles (29–35 km) a week. Over five months it builds you to a 45-mile (72 km) peak week and two 20-mile (32 km) long runs. Below is every week of the schedule in miles and kilometres, a pace key based on goal marathon pace, and how to adapt the plan.

Twenty weeks leaves room for a proper base phase, four cutback weeks and a three-week taper, without rushing the long runs. Not sure which plan? Compare them here.

Who this plan is for

  • You have run a half marathon, or 10 miles (16 km) or more continuously, in the last year.
  • You currently run 4–5 days a week, totalling 18–22 miles (29–35 km).
  • Your race is 20 weeks away and you want time to build gradually.
  • This might be your first marathon or your second. You want more than "just finish" but don't need an advanced plan.

If you already run 25–30 miles a week, the 16 week plan starts at your level. If you're below 15 miles a week, the 6 month plan or the beginner plan starts lower.

The full 20-week schedule (miles & km)

You run five days a week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. Tuesday is the main workout: hills, then threshold and intervals. From week 9, Thursday adds marathon-pace (MP) running. Sunday is the long run. Monday and Friday are rest days.

Pace key

  • Easy: conversational, about 60–90 s/mi (35–55 s/km) slower than goal marathon pace.
  • Long run: easy pace, 45–90 s/mi (30–55 s/km) slower than goal marathon pace, except segments marked @ MP.
  • MP: your goal marathon pace.
  • T (threshold): comfortably hard, the pace you could race for about an hour. Roughly 25–40 s/mi (15–25 s/km) faster than MP. Jog 2 min between reps.
  • I (intervals): 5K–10K effort, roughly 50–80 s/mi (30–50 s/km) faster than MP. Jog 90 s–2 min between reps.
  • Hills: 60 s uphill at 5K effort; jog back down.
  • Strides: 20 s quick and relaxed at the end of an easy run. Walk back to recover.
  • Workout distances include a 1–2 mi (2–3 km) warm-up and cool-down.

How the 20 weeks are built

  • Weeks 1–4, base: easy running, strides and short hill repeats to build strength. Mileage goes from 22 to 26 miles (35 to 42 km).
  • Weeks 5–8, build: threshold and interval sessions alternate on Tuesdays, and the long run reaches 13 miles (21 km).
  • Weeks 9–12, marathon pace: Thursday MP runs grow from 3 to 5 miles (5 to 8 km). Long runs reach 16 miles (26 km).
  • Weeks 13–17, peak: long runs of 17, 18 and 20 miles, then a cutback, then a second 20-miler in week 17. The week-17 peak is 45 miles (72 km).
  • Weeks 18–20, taper: 36, 29 and 13 miles (58, 47 and 21 km).

Cutback weeks fall in weeks 4, 8, 12 and 16. Weekly mileage never rises by more than 10%.

How to adjust the plan

  • Your race is 18 weeks away: start at week 3 if you already run about 25 miles (40 km) a week. Otherwise use the 18-week beginner plan.
  • Two 20-milers feel like too much: cut the week-15 long run to 18 miles (29 km) and keep week 17 at 20.
  • Four days a week: drop the Wednesday run. The peak becomes about 40 miles (64 km).
  • Goal pace: multiply your recent half-marathon time by about 2.1 to set MP, and add 5–10 minutes for a first marathon.
  • Missed a week: repeat the last full week you completed. Don't double up.
  • Pain or injury: pain that changes how you run, or doesn't ease within a few days, means stop and see a doctor or physio. Don't run through it.

Fueling, strength and race week

A 20-week block gives you more than a dozen long runs over 90 minutes, which is plenty of practice for race-day fueling. Use the same products every time. Keep strength work to two short sessions a week until the taper. Our guide to what a marathon plan should include has the details on carbohydrate targets, strength exercises and the taper.

FAQ

Is 20 weeks too long to train for a marathon?

No, if your starting base is modest. The extra four weeks compared with a 16-week plan go into base building and a second 20-miler. If you already run 30+ miles a week, 20 weeks can feel long, and a 16 week plan is usually enough.

Can a beginner use a 20 week marathon training plan?

Yes, if you have run a half marathon or can run 10 miles. If you are newer than that, use the 18-week beginner plan, which starts at 13 miles a week with four runs.

How many miles a week is a 20 week marathon plan?

This plan starts at 22 miles (35 km) and peaks at 45 miles (72 km) in week 17. Cutback weeks fall in between.

When should my longest run be?

Three weeks before race day, which is week 17 in this plan. That gives your body time to recover from it while the taper brings your freshness back.
keyTakeaway: Twenty weeks suits runners with a half marathon behind them and about 20 miles a week: a longer base, four cutback weeks and two 20-mile long runs.
